record: issue-77 single-corner diagnosis probe (simulated, pre-layout; NOT measured)
corner: typical / Vin 5.0 V / 27 C / no load (rload=1e9)
steady_state: not established: start-up transient only; Vout is still ~1.4-1.55 V (median over 50 us windows) at 700 us and the loop has not settled

observations.oscillator: clk 1.94 MHz at 300-400 us (194 rising edges in 100 us); ramp 0.98-1.81 V. In band; free-run spread of 0.02-3.2 MHz across units NOT reproduced or explained here (one corner only)

observations.vc_out_of_rail: vc reaches -0.92 V and +5.5 V with a 3.3 V control rail from ~180 us onward, coincident with ~ +/-2 V single-sample spikes on v(out) at SW edges (2.6% of samples outside -0.5..2.2 V in 300-700 us). Whether these spikes are physical or a bench-model artifact (out is the cap-side terminal; Cwind 3 pF/20 ohm, ESL 0.5 nH) is NOT traced

diagnosis: PARTIAL. At this corner the first block to depart from R15 intent is the PWM/compensator path (pwm held low ~140 us after the reference starts rising; vc driven far outside the 0-3.3 V rail by edge-synchronous coupling from v(out)), not the oscillator or the soft-start reference. The ideal-bias ports are not implicated at this corner. Design defect vs bench artifact for the out-node spikes is undecided; no spec row changed.
